text:
sam: Heads up — apiserver 5xx spike in us-west2 starting ~12:13 UTC. Controller-manager leader flips every ~10-18s. Noticed high etcd request latencies in the same window.

maya: seeing it in graphs too :eyes:. apiserver requestqueue depth shot up, lots of watch reconnects.

rory: log snippet from apiserver: ```E 12:13:22 apiserver.go:123] failed to list *v1.Pod: etcdserver: request timed out
W 12:13:25 watcher.go:87] watch chan closed: etcdserver: mvcc: required revision has been compacted```

pei: where are the events coming from? Any noisy controllers or mass pod restarts?

nora: checking node churn — GPU nodegroup had 14 node drains in last 8 minutes (autoscaler triggered due to spot terminations). Each drain is forcing reschedules of dozens of GPU workloads -> watch fanout is huge.

rory: that lines up. watch cache pressure + etcd i/o spikes means leader apply durations spike and controller-manager loses lease fast. Current leader-election lease is 15s which is too tight under this load.

maya: mitigation idea: temporarily pause cluster-autoscaler for the GPU nodegroup so we stop drains and let the system settle. Also bump controller-manager leaseDuration to 45s and renew. We can revert after load subsides.

sam: agreed — pause autoscaler now. Maya, can you open the CA change? I'll create a hotfix rollout for controller-manager with adjusted leader-election flags.

maya: done — paused GPU autoscaling via the CA configmap (scaleDown disabled) at 12:16 UTC.

nora: confirming reduced drain activity. Node churn rate falling.

rory: rolling restart for controller-manager started (image same, leader-elect flags overridden): `--leader-elect-lease-duration=45s --leader-elect-renew-deadline=30s` . Watching for stability.

infra-bot: Alert suppressed: apiserver high 5xx rate (us-west2) — suppression active until 1769999700.

pei: also recommend checking etcd disk iops on the affected raft peers — NVMe queue depth looked close to saturation yesterday during a scheduled backup. If iops are the bottleneck, reducing watch traffic is only a band-aid.

rory: good call. I/O graph for etcd leader peer spiked to 90% queue utilization at the spike. Opening ticket to raise EBS throttle or move etcd peers to higher-iops nodes: ENG-INFRA-4281.

sam: status check in 10m. If leader flips stop and 5xxs drop we keep config. If not, we'll failover etcd leader and (short-term) increase apiserver replicas behind LB.

nora: follow-up note — logs show a few controllers (custom GPU job scheduler) re-listing entire namespaces repeatedly after a crash loop. I'll escalate to the service team to add exponential backoff on reconnects to reduce watch churn.

maya: current metrics: apiserver 5xx rate down 85%, controller-manager leader holds stable for 2m. Looks like pause helped.

sam: nice work. Postmortem TODO: root cause seems to be spot termination-driven node churn -> many pod restarts -> watch/cache fanout -> etcd iops spike -> leader-election thrash. Need longer-term mitigations: tune CA for GPU spot pools, backoff in noisy controllers, increase etcd iops headroom or split heavy watchers to read replicas.

rory: adding cost note — permanently increasing etcd disk/instance class will raise infra spend ~6-8% for the cluster. Prefer improving autoscaler topology and controller behavior first.

sam: agreed. I'll schedule a deeper follow-up with infra and the GPU service team tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
